text:
sasha: quick PSA from profiler runs on the longctx chain-of-thought suite — we see very poor KV reuse across requests even when prefixes are identical. looks like keying is the culprit.
min: can you paste the profiler snippet?
sasha: gist: high miss rate for prefix entries, memory churn spikes, and a lot of small allocations during deserialization. top offender is the cache-key function that includes session_id and a rolling nonce.
arlo: wait — we intentionally added session_id to avoid cross-session collisions. Removing it could increase accidental reuse cross-tenant? :thinking:
sasha: good point. current keying: `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:%d", tenantID, sessionID, prefixHash)` — session scoping prevents reuse when the same user repeats prompts in a new session. proposal: separate prefix-priming keys that omit session_id and are marked as "shared-prefix" entries with strict tenant isolation (tenantID remains).
devon: so tenantID stays, but session_id dropped for prefix entries. that seems reasonable for multi-turn threads where the leading prompt portion is stable. what about eviction semantics? we don't want these priming entries to evict hot session-specific entries.
sasha: exactly. I'm proposing a dedicated small slab for priming entries with its own LRU and cap (e.g., 1–3% of KV pool). fallback path uses normal keying.
eva: can we instead use a two-level key: primaryKey = tenantID:prefixHash and secondaryKey = tenantID:sessionID:prefixHash and check primary first? that keeps backward compatibility and enables graceful fallback.
min: that increases lookup work per request (two probes). perf cost ok? microbench shows an extra probe is ~0.6-1.0µs on our hot path, should be acceptable if it reduces main compute by avoiding recompute. need numbers.
infra-bot: deploy-trace: perf/canary/1739876543 started — link: https://perf.internal/runs/1739876543
arlo: security check — ensure tenantID is authoritative and cannot be faked by a client. also log priming hits for auditing.
sasha: agreed. action plan: 1) implement priming slab + primaryKey probe (min's two-level flow) in runtime branch -> PR; 2) add metrics: priming_hit_rate, priming_evictions, priming_memory_bytes; 3) canary with 2% traffic for 48h; 4) rollback hook to disable primaryKey probe.
devon: add TTL for priming entries (e.g., 10s) to avoid longterm growth from noisy prefixes. also instrument size per entry to detect fragmentation (we saw many ~128B entries causing slab blowup).
eva: got a quick prototype for key derivation: ```func PrefixKey(tenant string, prefixHash uint64, shared bool) string { if shared { return fmt.Sprintf("p:%s:%d", tenant, prefixHash) } return fmt.Sprintf("s:%s:%d", tenant, prefixHash) }```
sasha: love it. next: I will open the PR and attach the profiler diff for the longctx suite. please review, esp. the eviction + telemetry parts.
min: will review tonight. if we can get priming_hit_rate > 40% on the longctx run with <2% extra mem, ship it.
arlo: don't forget to coordinate with security for the audit logs.
infra-bot: perf/canary/1739876543 completed: initial numbers posted to https://perf.internal/results/1739876543 (priming_hit_rate=0.0 for baseline).
sasha: note to self — baseline zeros are expected. PR will flip probe in canary to measure.
devon: fine-grained rollback: set env REDWOOD_PRIMING_MODE=off | probe-only | slab-only. that helps incident response.
sasha: perfect. I'll include that in the config and the rollout doc. thanks all :rocket:
